title: Giving false evidence
old_text: Defined giving false evidence as making a statement known or believed to be false while legally bound by oath or law to speak truth.
new_text: Defines giving false evidence as making any statement known or believed to be false while legally bound by oath or affirmation to state the truth.
punishment_old: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under IPC Section 193.
punishment_new: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under BNS Section 229.
explanation: Establishes the core definition of perjury under Indian penal law. Applies to oral testimony, written pleadings, and sworn affidavits. Renumbered from IPC Section 191.

title: Fabricating false evidence
old_text: Defined fabricating false evidence as creating false circumstances, entries, or records to mislead a judicial or public officer.
new_text: Defines fabricating false evidence as creating any false entry in a book, record, or electronic record, or staging false circumstances to deceive a judicial tribunal.
punishment_old: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under IPC Section 193.
punishment_new: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under BNS Section 229.
explanation: Penalizes planting false clues, altering accounts, or fabricating digital logs intended to produce an erroneous judicial opinion. Renumbered from IPC Section 192.

title: Punishment for false evidence
old_text: Penalized giving or fabricating false evidence in judicial proceedings with up to 7 years and fine; in other proceedings with up to 3 years and fine.
new_text: Whoever intentionally gives or fabricates false evidence in a judicial proceeding faces imprisonment up to seven years and fine; in other proceedings, imprisonment up to three years and fine.
punishment_old: Judicial: up to 7 years and fine; Non-judicial: up to 3 years and fine (IPC Section 193).
punishment_new: Judicial: imprisonment up to seven years, and fine; Non-judicial: imprisonment up to three years, and fine (BNS Section 229).
explanation: Prescribes sentencing for giving or fabricating false evidence, bifurcating between court proceedings and administrative inquiries. Renumbered from IPC Section 193.

title: Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence
old_text: Penalized fabricating false evidence to secure a death penalty conviction with life imprisonment or up to 10 years; if execution resulted, capital punishment.
new_text: Whoever gives or fabricates false evidence intending to procure capital conviction shall be punished with life imprisonment or rigorous imprisonment up to ten years and fine; if execution results, death or life imprisonment.
punishment_old: Life imprisonment or up to 10 years and fine; if innocent person executed: death or life imprisonment (IPC Section 194).
punishment_new: Imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment up to ten years, and fine; if execution occurs: death or life imprisonment (BNS Section 230).
explanation: Aggravated perjury aimed at causing the judicial execution of an innocent person. Retains capital punishment if execution was carried out. Renumbered from IPC Section 194.

title: Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of offence punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment
old_text: Penalized giving or fabricating false evidence to procure conviction of offences punishable with life imprisonment or imprisonment for 7+ years.
new_text: Whoever gives or fabricates false evidence with intent to procure conviction of an offence punishable with life imprisonment or 7+ years imprisonment faces the same punishment as that offence.
punishment_old: Punished in the same manner as an innocent person convicted of that offence would be liable (IPC Section 195).
punishment_new: Punished in the same manner as a person convicted of that offence would be liable (BNS Section 231).
explanation: Subjects malicious perjurers to the exact penalty prescribed for the grave crime they falsely attributed to the accused. Renumbered from IPC Section 195.

title: Threatening any person to give false evidence
old_text: Penalized threatening, intimidating, or inducing any person to give false evidence with imprisonment up to 7 years or fine; if innocent person convicted, matching punishment.
new_text: Whoever threatens another with injury to person, reputation or property to induce them to give false evidence faces imprisonment up to seven years and fine; if wrongful conviction ensues, matching punishment.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 7 years, or fine, or both; if conviction results, matching penalty (IPC Section 195A).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to seven years, or with fine, or with both; matching penalty if wrongful conviction occurs (BNS Section 232).
explanation: Criminalizes witness intimidation, threats, and coercion designed to corrupt court testimony. Renumbered from IPC Section 195A.

title: Using evidence known to be false
old_text: Penalized corruptly using or attempting to use evidence known to be false or fabricated as genuine evidence.
new_text: Whoever corruptly uses or attempts to use as true or genuine any evidence known to be false or fabricated shall be punished as if he gave or fabricated false evidence.
punishment_old: Punished in the same manner as giving or fabricating false evidence (IPC Section 196).
punishment_new: Punished in the same manner as giving or fabricating false evidence (BNS Section 233).
explanation: Targets litigants or prosecutors who introduce forged documents or coached testimony into trial records knowing them to be untrue. Renumbered from IPC Section 196.

title: Issuing or signing false certificate
old_text: Penalized issuing or signing any certificate admissible in evidence knowing it to be false in any material point.
new_text: Whoever issues or signs any certificate required by law or legally admissible in evidence, knowing or believing it to be false in any material point, shall be punished as for giving false evidence.
punishment_old: Punished in the same manner as giving false evidence (IPC Section 197).
punishment_new: Punished in the same manner as giving false evidence (BNS Section 234).
explanation: Penalizes doctors, engineers, public officials, or professionals signing bogus verification certificates used in evidence. Renumbered from IPC Section 197.

title: Using as true a certificate known to be false
old_text: Penalized corruptly using as genuine any certificate known to be false in a material point.
new_text: Whoever corruptly uses or attempts to use any certificate known to be false in any material point as a true certificate, shall be punished as for giving false evidence.
punishment_old: Punished in the same manner as giving false evidence (IPC Section 198).
punishment_new: Punished in the same manner as giving false evidence (BNS Section 235).
explanation: Penalizes presenting fabricated certificates before courts or public authorities to claim benefits or establish false facts. Renumbered from IPC Section 198.

title: False statement made in declaration which is by law receivable as evidence
old_text: Penalized making false statements in declarations receivable by law as evidence with punishment matching giving false evidence.
new_text: Whoever, in any declaration legally receivable as evidence, makes any statement known or believed to be false on a material point, shall be punished as for giving false evidence.
punishment_old: Punished in the same manner as giving false evidence (IPC Section 199).
punishment_new: Punished in the same manner as giving false evidence (BNS Section 236).
explanation: Criminalizes filing sworn false declarations, verification clauses in affidavits, and statutory declarations. Renumbered from IPC Section 199.

title: Using as true such declaration knowing it to be false
old_text: Penalized corruptly using as genuine any declaration receivable as evidence knowing it to be false in a material point.
new_text: Whoever corruptly uses or attempts to use as true any declaration receivable as evidence, knowing it to be false in any material point, shall be punished as for giving false evidence.
punishment_old: Punished in the same manner as giving false evidence (IPC Section 200).
punishment_new: Punished in the same manner as giving false evidence (BNS Section 237).
explanation: Penalizes tendering known false declarations in judicial proceedings. Clarifies that technical informality in the declaration does not bar liability. Renumbered from IPC Section 200.

title: Causing disappearance of evidence of offence, or giving false information to screen offender
old_text: Penalized destroying crime evidence or giving false information to screen offenders: if capital crime, up to 7 years; if life crime, up to 3 years; if other, 1/4 term.
new_text: Whoever causes evidence of an offence to disappear or gives false information to screen an offender: if capital crime, faces up to seven years and fine; if life imprisonment crime, up to three years and fine; other crimes, up to one-fourth the term.
punishment_old: Capital crime: up to 7 years and fine; Life crime: up to 3 years and fine; Other: up to 1/4 of longest term or fine (IPC Section 201).
punishment_new: Capital offence: imprisonment up to seven years, and fine; Life offence: imprisonment up to three years, and fine; Other offences: up to one-fourth term or fine or both (BNS Section 238).
explanation: The primary section punishing destruction of crime scenes, wiping CCTV footage, disposing of murder weapons, or misguiding investigators. Renumbered from IPC Section 201.

title: Intentional omission to give information of an offence by a person bound to inform
old_text: Penalized intentional failure by a person bound to inform to report an offence with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe an offence has been committed, intentionally omits to give information which he is legally bound to give, faces imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine, or both (IPC Section 202).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to six months, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 239).
explanation: Penalizes individuals under statutory reporting duties who remain silent to shield criminal acts. Renumbered from IPC Section 202.

title: Giving false information respecting an offence committed
old_text: Penalized knowingly giving false information respecting a committed offence with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe an offence has been committed, gives any information respecting that offence which he knows or believes to be false, faces imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 203).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to two years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 240).
explanation: Criminalizes feeding deceptive leads, fabricated witness narratives, or diversionary stories to police regarding a crime. Renumbered from IPC Section 203.

title: Destruction of document or electronic record to prevent its production as evidence
old_text: Penalized destroying or obliterating any document or electronic record to prevent its production as evidence with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever secrets or destroys any document or electronic record which he may be lawfully compelled to produce as evidence, with intent to prevent its production, faces imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 204).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to two years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 241).
explanation: Explicitly criminalizes deleting hard drives, shredding ledgers, or purging digital evidence under court subpoena. Renumbered from IPC Section 204.

title: False personation for the purpose of an act or proceeding in a suit or prosecution
old_text: Penalized falsely personating another and in such assumed character admitting judgment or doing an act in a lawsuit with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever falsely personates another and in such character confesses judgment, becomes bail, or does any act in a court suit or prosecution, faces imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 205).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to three years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 242).
explanation: Penalizes impersonating court litigants, standing fake bail sureties, or confessing judgments in another citizen's name. Renumbered from IPC Section 205.

title: Fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution
old_text: Penalized fraudulently removing or concealing property to avoid judicial forfeiture or decree execution with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever fraudulently removes, conceals or transfers property intending to prevent it from being taken in forfeiture or execution of a decree, faces imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 206).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to two years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 243).
explanation: Criminalizes transferring or spiriting away assets to defeat judicial attachment orders or court decrees. Renumbered from IPC Section 206.

title: Fraudulent claim to property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution
old_text: Penalized fraudulently claiming property knowing one has no right to it to prevent court seizure with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever fraudulently accepts, receives, or claims any property knowing he has no right to it, to prevent it from being taken in forfeiture or execution, faces imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 207).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to two years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 244).
explanation: Penalizes third parties who collude with judgment debtors by filing false ownership claims over attached property. Renumbered from IPC Section 207.

title: Fraudulently suffering a decree for a sum not due
old_text: Penalized fraudulently causing or suffering a court decree for a sum not due with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever fraudulently causes or suffers a decree or order to be passed against him at the suit of any person for a sum or property not due, faces imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 208).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to two years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 245).
explanation: Penalizes collusive lawsuits where debtors consent to bogus money decrees to shield wealth from legitimate creditors. Renumbered from IPC Section 208.

title: Dishonestly making a false claim in Court
old_text: Penalized fraudulently or dishonestly making any claim in a court of justice known to be false with imprisonment up to 2 years and fine.
new_text: Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly, or with intent to injure or annoy any person, makes in a Court of Justice any claim which he knows to be false, shall be punished with imprisonment up to two years, and fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, and fine (IPC Section 209).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to two years, and shall also be liable to fine (BNS Section 246).
explanation: Crucial provision targeting vexatious litigants and extortionate plaintiffs filing false civil or criminal plaints. Renumbered from IPC Section 209.

title: Fraudulently obtaining a decree for a sum not due
old_text: Penalized fraudulently obtaining a decree or order for a sum not due or already satisfied with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever fraudulently obtains a decree or order against any person for a sum not due, or after a decree has been satisfied causes it to be executed, faces imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 210).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to two years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 247).
explanation: Penalizes obtaining court orders for fabricated debts or re-executing decrees that have already been discharged. Renumbered from IPC Section 210.

title: False charge of an offence made with intent to injure
old_text: Penalized instituting false criminal proceedings or falsely charging an offence with intent to injure with up to 2 years or fine; if capital/life crime falsely charged, up to 7 years and fine.
new_text: Whoever institutes false criminal proceedings or falsely charges any person with an offence knowing there is no just ground: faces imprisonment up to two years or fine; if capital, life, or 7+ years crime falsely charged, faces imprisonment up to seven years and fine.
punishment_old: General: up to 2 years, or fine, or both; Capital/life/7+ years false charge: up to 7 years and fine (IPC Section 211).
punishment_new: General: imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both; Capital/life/7+ years false charge: imprisonment up to seven years, and fine (BNS Section 248).
explanation: The benchmark section punishing malicious prosecution and lodging bogus criminal FIRs to harass innocent citizens. Renumbered from IPC Section 211.

title: Harbouring an offender
old_text: Penalized harbouring or concealing an offender to screen them from arrest: if capital crime, up to 5 years; if life crime, up to 3 years; if other, 1/4 term, with spousal exception.
new_text: Whoever harbours or conceals a person whom he knows or has reason to believe to be an offender, with intent to screen him from legal punishment: if capital offence, faces up to five years and fine; if life offence, up to three years and fine; other offences, up to one-fourth term. Spouses exempt.
punishment_old: Capital: up to 5 years and fine; Life: up to 3 years and fine; Other: up to 1/4 term or fine (IPC Section 212).
punishment_new: Capital: imprisonment up to five years, and fine; Life: imprisonment up to three years, and fine; Other: up to one-fourth of longest term or fine (BNS Section 249).
explanation: Penalizes operating criminal safehouses to shield fugitives from arrest, while maintaining the marital exception for spouses. Renumbered from IPC Section 212.

title: Taking a gift, etc., to screen an offender from punishment
old_text: Penalized accepting any gift or gratification in consideration of screening an offender: if capital crime, up to 7 years; if life crime, up to 3 years; other, 1/4 term.
new_text: Whoever accepts or agrees to accept gratification in consideration of concealing an offence or screening any person from legal punishment: if capital crime, faces up to seven years and fine; if life crime, up to three years and fine; other crimes, up to one-fourth term.
punishment_old: Capital: up to 7 years and fine; Life: up to 3 years and fine; Other: up to 1/4 term or fine (IPC Section 213).
punishment_new: Capital offence: imprisonment up to seven years, and fine; Life offence: imprisonment up to three years, and fine; Other: up to one-fourth term or fine (BNS Section 250).
explanation: Penalizes witnesses or complainants accepting hush-money to conceal crimes or screen perpetrators. Renumbered from IPC Section 213.

title: Offering gift or restoration of property in consideration of screening offender
old_text: Penalized giving or offering gratification in consideration of screening an offender with matching penalties to receiving such gift.
new_text: Whoever gives or offers gratification to any person in consideration of screening an offender or not proceeding against him: if capital crime, faces up to seven years; if life crime, up to three years; other crimes, up to one-fourth term.
punishment_old: Capital: up to 7 years and fine; Life: up to 3 years and fine; Other: up to 1/4 term or fine (IPC Section 214).
punishment_new: Capital offence: imprisonment up to seven years, and fine; Life offence: imprisonment up to three years, and fine; Other: up to one-fourth term or fine (BNS Section 251).
explanation: Penalizes the person offering hush-money or settlement bribes to hush up serious non-compoundable crimes. Renumbered from IPC Section 214.

title: Taking gift to help to recover stolen property, etc.
old_text: Penalized taking gratification under pretence of helping recover stolen property without causing apprehension of the offender with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever takes or agrees to take gratification under pretence of helping recover stolen property, unless he uses all means in his power to cause the offender to be apprehended, faces imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 215).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to two years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 252).
explanation: Penalizes middlemen and underworld fixers who collect fees to 'recover' stolen vehicles or goods without helping police arrest the thieves. Renumbered from IPC Section 215.

title: Harbouring offender who has escaped from custody or whose apprehension has been ordered
old_text: Penalized harbouring a person who escaped lawful custody or whose arrest was ordered: if capital crime, up to 7 years; if life crime, up to 3 years; other, 1/4 term. Spouses exempt.
new_text: Whoever harbours a person who has escaped from lawful custody or whose arrest has been ordered: if capital offence, faces up to seven years and fine; if life offence, up to three years and fine; other crimes, up to one-fourth term. Spouses exempt.
punishment_old: Capital: up to 7 years and fine; Life: up to 3 years and fine; Other: up to 1/4 term or fine (IPC Section 216).
punishment_new: Capital offence: imprisonment up to seven years, and fine; Life offence: imprisonment up to three years, and fine; Other: up to one-fourth term or fine (BNS Section 253).
explanation: Penalizes harbouring escaped prison convicts or proclaimed fugitives carrying active arrest warrants. Renumbered from IPC Section 216.

title: Penalty for harbouring robbers or dacoits
old_text: Penalized knowingly harbouring persons about to commit robbery or dacoity with rigorous imprisonment up to 7 years and fine, with spousal exception.
new_text: Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe that any persons are about to commit or have recently committed robbery or dacoity, harbours them, faces rigorous imprisonment up to seven years, and fine. Spouses exempt.
punishment_old: Rigorous imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine (IPC Section 216A).
punishment_new: Rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine (BNS Section 254).
explanation: Targeted anti-dacoity provision penalizing persons who furnish safehouses, arms, or sustenance to armed robbery gangs. Renumbered from IPC Section 216A.

title: Public servant disobeying direction of law with intent to save person from punishment or property from forfeiture
old_text: Penalized a public servant disobeying directions of law with intent to save an accused from punishment or property from forfeiture with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever, being a public servant, knowingly disobeys any direction of law regarding his official conduct, intending to save any person from punishment or property from forfeiture, faces imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 217).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to two years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 255).
explanation: Penalizes corrupt police or public officers who intentionally botch procedures to protect favored criminals from conviction. Renumbered from IPC Section 217.

title: Public servant framing incorrect record or writing with intent to save person from punishment or property from forfeiture
old_text: Penalized a public servant framing an incorrect record or writing to save an offender from punishment or property from forfeiture with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever, being a public servant charged with preparing records, intentionally frames them incorrectly to save any person from punishment or property from forfeiture, faces imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 218).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to three years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 256).
explanation: Penalizes falsifying official police diaries, forensic reports, or land registries to shield suspects from criminal liability. Renumbered from IPC Section 218.

title: Public servant in judicial proceeding corruptly making report, etc., contrary to law
old_text: Penalized a public servant corruptly or maliciously making any report, order, verdict, or decision in a judicial proceeding contrary to law with imprisonment up to 7 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever, being a public servant, corruptly or maliciously makes or pronounces in any stage of a judicial proceeding any report, order, verdict, or decision which he knows to be contrary to law, faces imprisonment up to seven years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 7 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 219).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to seven years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 257).
explanation: Guarantees judicial probity by penalizing corrupt judges, magistrates, or court officials issuing knowingly unlawful orders. Renumbered from IPC Section 219.

title: Commitment for trial or confinement by person having authority who knows that he is acting contrary to law
old_text: Penalized corruptly committing any person for trial or confinement contrary to law with imprisonment up to 7 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever, in any office which gives him authority to commit persons for trial or confinement, corruptly or maliciously commits any person for trial or keeps them in confinement contrary to law, faces imprisonment up to seven years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 7 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 220).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to seven years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 258).
explanation: Protects personal liberty against tyrannical judicial or police officers who remand innocent citizens to jail knowing it violates the law. Renumbered from IPC Section 220.

title: Intentional omission to apprehend on the part of public servant bound to apprehend
old_text: Penalized intentional failure by a public servant bound to arrest: if capital crime, up to 7 years; if life/10+ years crime, up to 3 years; other, up to 2 years.
new_text: Whoever, being a public servant legally bound to apprehend any person charged with or liable to be apprehended for an offence, intentionally omits to apprehend him: if capital crime, faces up to seven years; if life crime, up to three years; other crimes, up to two years.
punishment_old: Capital: up to 7 years and fine; Life/10+ years: up to 3 years or fine; Other: up to 2 years or fine (IPC Section 221).
punishment_new: Capital offence: imprisonment up to seven years, with or without fine; Life offence: up to three years, with or without fine; Other: up to two years, with or without fine (BNS Section 259).
explanation: Penalizes police officers who intentionally let wanted criminals slip away rather than arresting them. Renumbered from IPC Section 221.

title: Intentional omission to apprehend on the part of public servant bound to apprehend person under sentence or lawfully committed
old_text: Penalized intentional omission by a public servant to apprehend a person under sentence or lawfully committed: if capital sentence, life or up to 14 years; if life/10+ years sentence, up to 7 years; other, up to 3 years.
new_text: Whoever, being a public servant bound to apprehend a person under sentence of a Court, intentionally omits to apprehend: if under capital sentence, faces life imprisonment or up to 14 years; if under life sentence, up to seven years; other sentences, up to three years.
punishment_old: Capital convict: life imprisonment or up to 14 years; Life convict: up to 7 years; Other: up to 3 years or fine (IPC Section 222).
punishment_new: Capital convict: imprisonment for life or up to fourteen years, and fine; Life convict: up to seven years and fine; Other: up to three years or fine (BNS Section 260).
explanation: Imposes severe sentences on jailers or police escorts who intentionally fail to apprehend convicted felons. Renumbered from IPC Section 222.

title: Escape from confinement or custody resulting from negligence on the part of public servant
old_text: Penalized a public servant who negligently suffered an accused or convict in custody to escape with simple imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever, being a public servant legally bound to keep in confinement any person charged with or convicted of an offence, negligently suffers such person to escape, faces simple imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Simple imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 223).
punishment_new: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 261).
explanation: Penalizes police guards and jail sentries whose gross carelessness or sleep on duty allows prisoners to escape. Renumbered from IPC Section 223.

title: Resistance or obstruction by a person to his lawful apprehension
old_text: Penalized intentionally offering resistance or obstruction to one's own lawful arrest, or escaping from custody, with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever intentionally offers resistance or illegal obstruction to the lawful apprehension of himself for any offence, or escapes or attempts to escape from lawful custody, faces imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 224).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to two years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 262).
explanation: Penalizes suspects resisting police arrest or prisoners breaking out of lockup or police custody. Renumbered from IPC Section 224.

title: Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension of another person
old_text: Penalized intentionally offering resistance or obstruction to the arrest of another, or rescuing another from custody: up to 2 years or fine; if capital offence accused, up to 7 years; if life convict rescued, life or up to 10 years.
new_text: Whoever resists or obstructs the lawful apprehension of another, or rescues another from lawful custody: faces up to two years or fine; if the person was charged with capital offence, up to seven years and fine; if under sentence of death, life imprisonment or up to ten years and fine.
punishment_old: General: up to 2 years or fine; Capital charged: up to 7 years and fine; Death sentence convict: life or up to 10 years and fine (IPC Section 225).
punishment_new: General: up to two years or fine; Capital charged: up to seven years and fine; Death sentence convict: imprisonment for life or up to ten years, and fine (BNS Section 263).
explanation: Penalizes mob attacks on police vehicles or rescuing accomplices from judicial custody. Renumbered from IPC Section 225.

title: Omission to apprehend, or sufferance of escape, on part of public servant in cases not otherwise provided for
old_text: Penalized omission to apprehend or suffering escape by a public servant where not otherwise provided for: if intentional, up to 3 years or fine; if negligent, simple imprisonment up to 2 years or fine.
new_text: Whoever, being a public servant bound to apprehend or keep in custody any person, omits to apprehend or suffers escape in cases not otherwise provided for: if intentional, faces up to three years or fine; if negligent, simple imprisonment up to two years or fine.
punishment_old: Intentional: up to 3 years or fine or both; Negligent: simple imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both (IPC Section 225A).
punishment_new: Intentional: imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both; Negligent: simple imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both (BNS Section 264).
explanation: Residual clause punishing public servants for omissions regarding escapes where special provisions do not apply. Renumbered from IPC Section 225A.

title: Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension, or escape or rescue in cases not otherwise provided for
old_text: Penalized resistance, obstruction, escape, or rescue in cases not otherwise provided for with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to ₹1,000, or both.
new_text: Whoever, in any case not otherwise provided for, intentionally resists or obstructs lawful apprehension, or escapes from custody, shall be punished with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both (IPC Section 225B).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to six months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both (BNS Section 265).
explanation: Residual provision penalizing obstruction to civil arrests, execution of civil warrants, or escape from civil confinement, raising the fine to ₹5,000. Renumbered from IPC Section 225B.

title: Violation of condition of remission of punishment
old_text: Penalized violation of any condition of conditional remission or pardon by subjecting the offender to the unexpired portion of the original sentence.
new_text: Whoever, having accepted any conditional remission of punishment, knowingly violates any condition on which such remission was granted, shall be punished with the unexpired portion of his original sentence.
punishment_old: Punished with so much of the sentence as has not been served (IPC Section 227).
punishment_new: Remanded to undergo the unexpired portion of the original sentence (BNS Section 266).
explanation: Enforces conditions of executive pardons and remissions, canceling release and restoring the original sentence upon breach. Renumbered from IPC Section 227.

title: Intentional insult or interruption to public servant sitting in judicial proceeding
old_text: Penalized intentional insult or interruption to a public servant sitting in a judicial proceeding with simple imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to ₹1,000, or both.
new_text: Whoever intentionally offers any insult, or causes any interruption to any public servant, while such public servant is sitting in any stage of a judicial proceeding, shall be punished with simple imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both.
punishment_old: Simple imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both (IPC Section 228).
punishment_new: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both (BNS Section 267).
explanation: Protects courtroom decorum and judicial dignity by penalizing insults or disruptions before sitting judges, raising the fine fivefold to ₹5,000. Renumbered from IPC Section 228.

title: Personation of an assessor
old_text: Penalized personation or fraudulently procuring oneself to be empanelled or sworn as a jury or assessor with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever, by personation or otherwise, intentionally causes himself to be returned, empanelled or sworn as an assessor, knowing he is not entitled by law, shall be punished with imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years, or with fine, or with both (IPC Section 229).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to two years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 268).
explanation: Penalizes fraudulently infiltrating a judicial tribunal by impersonating an assessor. Renumbered from IPC Section 229.

title: Failure by person released on bail bond or bond to appear in Court
old_text: Penalized failure by a person released on bail or bond to appear in court without sufficient cause with imprisonment up to 1 year or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever, having been charged with an offence and released on bail bond or on bond, fails without sufficient cause (the burden of proof lying on him) to appear in Court, shall be punished with imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both, in addition to bond forfeiture (IPC Section 229A).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to one year, or with fine, or with both, in addition to bond forfeiture (BNS Section 269).
explanation: Specifically penalizes bail-jumping. Clarifies that the burden of proving sufficient cause rests squarely on the accused, and punishment is additive to bond forfeiture. Concludes Chapter XIV. Renumbered from IPC Section 229A.
